title: The installer writes the pre-commit hook only inside the target's own .git directory (A20)

context.task: Close A20: the installer joins the target with git's answer for hooks/pre-commit lexically, so an absolute or escaping hooks path writes the kit's pre-commit outside the target, where it can block every other repository's commits.

select.heading: A20 — El instalador escribe el `pre-commit` fuera del destino

problem: plan_pre_commit does `destination = target / shown`, with `shown` the output of `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-commit`. An absolute core.hooksPath (a global one shared by every repository of the user) makes `shown` absolute, and `target / '/abs'` is `/abs`; a relative one like `../shared` leaves the target too. blocked() only examines ancestors whose parents include the target, so it sees neither. The installer then writes the kit's pre-commit outside the target (promise I1 broken); in a shared hooks directory that hook runs in every repository of the user, finds no tools/git/commit_integrity.py there and refuses every commit (CASES.md, A20, reproduced with --dry-run in a throwaway HOME). Two more cases put the hook out of the target's own git directory: a linked worktree or a target whose .git is a file (a submodule, or `git init --separate-git-dir`), whose hooks belong to another repository; and a hooks path inside the working tree (core.hooksPath=custom-hooks, .husky/_), where the agent can rewrite the hook that runs as the person.
decisions: D1 The destination stays what `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-commit` says (it honours core.hooksPath); what changes is where it may be.

D2 The hook may be written only inside the target's own git directory: `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`, resolved, must be `<target>/.git` and a real directory (not a symbolic link, not reached through a `.git` file); and the destination, resolved with os.path.realpath (which follows the links of every existing ancestor), must be inside that directory. Anything else is a conflict on the hook's label: nothing is written (I2) and the exit status is 1, with --dry-run as well.

D3 A hooks path inside the working tree is refused too: `.git` is what Claude Code's sandbox protects from Bash, while a hooks directory in the working tree is writable by the agent, and the pre-commit runs as the person. Accepted by the author on 2026-10-13: a project whose hooks live in the working tree (.husky) wires the kit's pre-commit by hand.

D4 The conflict's reason names the resolved destination and the cause: when `git config --get core.hooksPath` gives a value, that core.hooksPath (with its value) puts the hooks outside <target>/.git, and the way out is to unset it or to wire the kit's pre-commit into those hooks by hand; when the git directory is not <target>/.git, the target is a linked worktree or has its git directory elsewhere (a submodule, --separate-git-dir), its hooks are shared with another repository, and the way out is to install from the main working tree. One reason per conflict, on one line, in the installer's existing conflict format.
D5 git runs through the installer's existing git() helper and tools.audit.run_process, as today; no new process primitive.

D6 Nothing else changes: the other plan steps, the report, the warnings, the checks of check_target, and a normal repository, which installs into .git/hooks/pre-commit exactly as today. A core.hooksPath that resolves inside <target>/.git is accepted.

D7 Tests configure git only through the throwaway HOME of make_home and environment() (for a global core.hooksPath, its .gitconfig) or the target's own repository configuration; never the person's git configuration, and never a directory outside tmp_path.

D8 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.
D9 This contract is launched first of the three that stay in the v0.1 (A20, A31, A34; author, 2026-10-15); its base commit is stamped at launch.

D10 The session's validator requires a Rationale in every proposal (AGENTS.md 2.2). The schema of validate_proposal shown in this session may be an older copy without it: include it anyway, or the proposal comes back INVALID_JSON.

behaviours.statement: With a global core.hooksPath that is an absolute directory outside the target (in the throwaway HOME's .gitconfig), the installer reports a conflict on the hook naming the resolved directory and core.hooksPath, writes nothing in the target nor in that directory, and exits 1; with --dry-run it reports the same conflict and exits 1.
With a repository core.hooksPath that leaves the target (`../shared-hooks`), the same conflict, nothing written anywhere, exit 1.
With a repository core.hooksPath inside the working tree (`custom-hooks`), a conflict naming it (D3), nothing written, exit 1.

With a linked worktree as the target (made with `git worktree add`), a conflict saying its git directory is not <target>/.git; nothing written in the worktree nor in the main repository's .git, exit 1.
With a target whose .git is a file pointing to a git directory elsewhere (`git init --separate-git-dir`, the shape of a submodule), the same conflict as B4, nothing written, exit 1.

A normal repository, and one whose core.hooksPath resolves inside its own .git, install the hook there with the kit's bytes and mode 0755, as today; a target whose .git/hooks is a symbolic link is still a conflict; a second run after a successful install changes nothing (I3).

tests.must_catch: a hook written outside the target through an absolute global core.hooksPath, or a dry run that does not report it
tests.reason: today plan_pre_commit writes to the shared directory and exits 0

tests.must_catch: a hook written outside the target through a relative core.hooksPath that escapes it
tests.reason: today `target / '../shared-hooks/pre-commit'` is written and the install exits 0

tests.must_catch: a hook written into a hooks directory of the working tree
tests.reason: today the hook goes to custom-hooks/ and the existing test asserts it; that test now expects the conflict

tests.must_catch: a hook written into another repository's .git from a linked worktree target
tests.reason: today git's answer points into the main repository's .git and the installer writes there

tests.must_catch: a hook written into a git directory outside the target when .git is a file
tests.reason: today git's answer is absolute, outside the target, and the installer writes there

tests.must_catch: a change to a normal install, to a core.hooksPath inside .git, to the refusal of a symbolically linked .git/hooks, or to idempotence
tests.reason: these already behave as B6 at the base commit and must keep doing so
